topic.title: Polynomial Functions and End Behavior
topic.summary: Limit notation for end behavior and why the degree and the sign of the leading term determine the end behavior of a polynomial function.

lesson.title: Polynomial Functions and End Behavior
lesson.summary: Limit notation for end behavior and why the degree and the sign of the leading term determine the end behavior of a polynomial function.
learningGoals: 1.6.A Describe end behaviors of polynomial functions.
lesson.bigIdea: As input values increase or decrease without bound, the leading term of a polynomial dominates all lower-degree terms. So the degree and the sign of the leading term determine the end behavior.
lesson.context: Zeros and extrema describe the middle of a polynomial's graph. End behavior describes the output values as the input values increase or decrease without bound, and the AP Exam expects it in limit notation.

sections.title: 1.6.A · End behavior is written with limit notation.

blocks.text: As the input values of a nonconstant polynomial function p increase without bound, the output values either increase without bound or decrease without bound. The corresponding notation is lim x→∞ p(x) = ∞ or lim x→∞ p(x) = −∞. As the input values decrease without bound, the output values also either increase or decrease without bound: lim x→−∞ p(x) = ∞ or lim x→−∞ p(x) = −∞.

blocks.caption: End behavior of four power functions

blocks.text: The symbols ∞ and −∞ describe output values that increase or decrease without bound. They are not output values the function reaches.

sections.takeaway: The input direction goes under lim, and the output behavior goes after the equals sign.

sections.title: 1.6.A · The leading term dominates for input values of large magnitude.

blocks.text: The degree and sign of the leading term of a polynomial determine its end behavior, because as the input values increase or decrease without bound, the values of the leading term dominate the values of all lower-degree terms. In p(x) = x³ − 100x², the term −100x² is larger in magnitude for small x, but x³ takes over as x grows.
At x = 10,000, p(x) is 99% of x³. The end behavior of p is the end behavior of x³: lim x→∞ p(x) = ∞ and lim x→−∞ p(x) = −∞.

sections.takeaway: A polynomial has the end behavior of its leading term.

sections.title: 1.6.A · The degree and the sign of the leading coefficient give four cases.

blocks.caption: End behavior from the leading term aₙxⁿ

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: For p(x) = −2x⁴ + 5x³ − x: the leading term −2x⁴ has a negative sign and an even degree; therefore, lim x→−∞ p(x) = −∞ and lim x→∞ p(x) = −∞.
Real zeros, relative extrema, and points of inflection describe the middle of the graph. They never change the end behavior, which depends only on the leading term.

blocks.caption: Graph of p(x) = −2x⁴ + 5x³ − x: both ends decrease without bound
blocks.alt: A quartic curve that comes up from the bottom left, has a few turns near the origin, and goes back down at the bottom right.

sections.takeaway: Even degree: both ends go the same way. Odd degree: the ends go opposite ways. The sign of the leading coefficient sets the direction as x → ∞.

vocabulary.definition: The degree and sign of the leading term of a polynomial determines the end behavior of the polynomial function, because as the input values increase or decrease without bound, the values of the leading term dominate the values of all lower-degree terms.

connections.title: Even and odd powers
connections.body: Topic 1.5 showed that p(x) = aₙxⁿ is even when n is even and odd when n is odd. That same parity decides whether the two ends of a polynomial's graph point the same way.
connections.transferQuestion: Why do x² and x⁴ have ends that point the same way?
connections.feedback: A negative number raised to an even power is positive, so input values of large magnitude on either side give large positive output values.

connections.title: Comparing leading terms in a quotient
connections.body: Topic 1.7 finds the end behavior of a rational function by examining the quotient of the leading terms of the numerator and the denominator.
connections.transferQuestion: What would you compare to find the end behavior of a quotient of two polynomials?
connections.feedback: The leading terms of the numerator and denominator, since they dominate for input values of large magnitude.

glossary.definition: A nonconstant polynomial function of x is any function representation that is equivalent to the analytical form p(x) = aₙxⁿ + aₙ₋₁xⁿ⁻¹ + aₙ₋₂xⁿ⁻² + … + a₂x² + a₁x + a₀, where n is a positive integer, aᵢ is a real number for each i from 0 to n, and aₙ is nonzero. A nonzero constant is also a polynomial function of degree zero.
The polynomial has degree n, the leading term is aₙxⁿ, and the leading coefficient is aₙ.
